text:
sam: Quick prototype question — I'm working on a tiny per-route dashboard card that surfaces: pinned model version, current routing policy (primary/fallback), 1h latency P95, and an inline cost estimate. Thinking about where the "saved filter" affordance should live. Should we tie saved filters to the route, the model, or keep them global?
mira: my vote is route-scoped by default. Most people land on a route and expect their filters to be relevant to that route only. global saves get messy fast. :+1:
chen: agree route-default, but we need a clear export path. If a user wants to promote a route-saved-query to org-wide, there should be a simple button that rewrites scope and validates tokens/permission.
alex: heads-up: route-scoped saves interact with quota previews — if we show an inline cost estimate the scope determines sampling/preview tokens. We should avoid surprises (e.g. saved query that implicitly switches to a heavier model causing cost spike). Maybe show a lightweight preview modal with sample token counts.
sam: good point. I'm thinking small UX: a kebab menu on the card with "Save view" -> modal radio: [Save for this route] [Save across org]. Default = route. Show estimated token burn for the sample timeframe.
julia: +1 for radio. Also consider the rollout case: if a route is pinned to a canary model, do saved views lock the model version? Users might expect a saved filter to also pin the model version they tested with. We need to be explicit.
chen: API contract concern: what fields does the saved-view object include? suggestion: {"scope": "route|org", "route_id": "...", "pinned_model": "model@sha?", "query": "...", "sample_window": "1h", "sample_rate": 0.01}. Need to document sampling semantics.
alex: + schema looks fine. but note: pinned_model must be optional to allow "follow current route pin" semantics. if omitted, render view with the route's live pin and show a banner: "This view follows route pin — model may change."
infra-bot: deploy: feature/route-mini-dashboard -> staging succeeded in 3m 12s.
mira: UX nit: saved queries list should surface whether a view pins a model or follows. small tag: [pins vX] or [follows route]. Also permissioning — org admins should be able to see route saves? probably yes, but editing could be restricted.
sam: permission Q — should we let a non-admin save an org-scoped view? probably not. propose: only users with "manage-views" can create org-scoped saves. Everyone can create route-scoped saves if they have read access.
chen: agree. Add server-side validation: if user attempts org scope without permission return 403. Keep UI optimistic but fall back with a clear error.
julia: regarding telemetry: every time a saved view is loaded we need to emit a telemetry event with fields {view_id, scope, pinned_model?, route_id?, sample_window, user_id} — so we can detect regressions tied to views. Also track whether the view caused a routing fallback (e.g., primary model rejected -> fallback used).
alex: one more edge: exporting a route-saved-view to a dashboard (embed) needs a stable URL including view_id and a read-only token option. we should discuss token expiry and audits in the console.
sam: OK action items: 1) I'll wire the modal with radio + preview token burn + note about pin vs follow. 2) chen — draft saved-view API schema + validation rules. 3) julia — telemetry events spec for load + routing fallback + cost-preview. 4) mira/alex — permission matrix for create/edit/share. I'll open PR for the prototype in staging and link it here.
mira: sweet, thanks. one more: label the card header "Route snapshot" not "dashboard" — keeps it light.
sam: noted. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/8912
alex: I'll review the API schema tomorrow morning.
chen: I'll sketch the sample payload and post here in a follow-up.
sam: thanks all. :rocket:
